seo.meta_title: Peter Luger Las Vegas: Hours, Credit Cards and What to Order
seo.meta_description: Peter Luger Steak House at Caesars Palace opened in 2023. Hours, reservations, how it differs from Brooklyn, credit cards, and the Vegas-only shellfish tower.
seo.h1: Peter Luger Las Vegas at Caesars Palace

question: What to Know About Peter Luger Las Vegas
quick_answer: Peter Luger Steak House Las Vegas is inside Caesars Palace on the Strip, next to MR CHOW. It opened in October 2023 as the Brooklyn steakhouse's first U.S. location outside New York. It's open 5 to 10 p.m. on Mondays and Tuesdays and 11:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday, takes reservations through OpenTable and Caesars, and, unlike the original, accepts credit cards. The menu mirrors Brooklyn's, led by the dry-aged porterhouse, plus a Vegas-only chilled shellfish tower.
key_facts: Inside Caesars Palace, next to MR CHOW

body.heading: Where it is and when it opened
body.text: Peter Luger Las Vegas sits inside Caesars Palace at 3570 Las Vegas Blvd. South, beside MR CHOW. It was first announced in January 2022 for a late-2022 opening, slipped to 2023, began serving in mid-October 2023 and held its official grand opening on November 10, 2023. Caesars called it Peter Luger's fourth location worldwide, after Brooklyn, Great Neck, New York, and Tokyo, its first new U.S. restaurant in more than 60 years and its first outside New York.

body.heading: Hours and reservations
body.text: Listed hours are 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. on Mondays and Tuesdays, when it serves dinner only, and 11:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday, when lunch is also served. It regularly shows up among OpenTable's most-booked Las Vegas restaurants, so booking ahead is a good idea. Reservations are taken on OpenTable and through the Caesars Palace website, and the restaurant's phone number is (702) 731-7267. Holiday hours can change.

body.heading: Yes, it takes credit cards
body.text: Peter Luger in Brooklyn is famous for refusing credit cards for decades, accepting cash, debit cards, checks and its own house card instead. The Las Vegas location broke that rule from the start and accepts major credit cards, which makes it easier for visitors.

body.heading: What's on the menu
body.text: Peter Luger said it wanted Las Vegas to have the same menu, the same feel and the same quality beef as New York. The star is the USDA Prime dry-aged porterhouse, sliced and served sizzling for two, three or four. A dry-aging room was built at Caesars so the beef is aged on site. Classic sides and starters include the extra-thick bacon, creamed spinach and German fried potatoes. The one Vegas exclusive is a chilled shellfish tower with shrimp, oysters, Maine lobster and king crab. For Brooklyn prices, see our Peter Luger menu page.

body.heading: What it feels like
body.text: The room was designed by Jeffrey Beers International to echo the Brooklyn original, with exposed brick, wood paneling, oak floors and tables and industrial-style windows. A display kitchen lets diners watch the chefs work. Expect a high bill: it's a premium Strip steakhouse, and OpenTable lists it at $50 and over per person before drinks.

faqs.q: Is there a Peter Luger in Las Vegas?
faqs.a: Yes. Peter Luger Steak House Las Vegas is inside Caesars Palace on the Strip and opened in October 2023.

faqs.q: Does Peter Luger Las Vegas take credit cards?
faqs.a: Yes. Unlike the Brooklyn original, the Las Vegas location accepts major credit cards.

faqs.q: What are Peter Luger Las Vegas hours?
faqs.a: Listed hours are 5–10 p.m. Monday and Tuesday and 11:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday.

faqs.q: Is the Las Vegas menu the same as Brooklyn?
faqs.a: Mostly. It follows the New York menu, and adds a chilled shellfish tower you can't get in New York.

faqs.q: Do you need a reservation at Peter Luger Las Vegas?
faqs.a: It's strongly recommended. You can book on OpenTable or through Caesars Palace.
